subject: Post-demo: hosted pricing follow-up & burst/peak profile
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: hosted pricing follow-up & burst/peak profile

Hi Lisa — great to meet yesterday and thanks for walking us through Acme's product flows. Quick recap from our side and three asks so we can get you a clean hosted quote (and a short runway estimate for SLA sizing):

Summary of what you told us on the call
- Primary feature: contextual assist inside Acme Editor (user prompts + model responses).
- Typical request payload (median): ~1,200 tokens (prompt + expected response); exploratory flows sometimes go to ~2,500 tokens.
- Monthly run rate (you estimated): somewhere between 30M and 60M tokens/month in the first 6 months as you scale pilots.
- Peak concurrency: production traffic during marketing pushes could see short bursts; your engineering note said sustained production peaks ~50 req/s and brief experiments up to ~120 req/s for 5–15 minute windows.

What we need to validate to size pricing and SLA options
1) Confirm a conservative monthly expectation (pick low/likely/high): 30M / 45M / 60M tokens.
2) Confirm whether the 120 req/s bursts are expected to be full production (customer-facing) or internal experiments. Duration estimate for bursts (minutes/hours/day).
3) Share a week-long sample of per-minute traffic if possible (CSV attachment format suggested).

Quick cost orientation (high level)
- With an average call ~1,200 tokens, 50 req/s sustained ~= 60k tokens/sec at peak short windows; that maps to roughly 5.2B tokens/month if that sustained level held constantly, so we size on bursts and sustained separately.
- Typical hosted banding: pay-as-you-go list price, discounted volume bands for committed monthly units, and reserved capacity for predictable sustained TPS.

Next steps
- If you can confirm the low/likely/high monthly numbers and drop a short sample (per-minute) CSV, Marissa will put together 2 pricing options: (A) pay-as-you-go with volume bands; (B) 12-month reserved slab with burst buffer and a target $/1M tokens.

I've attached a suggested sample CSV schema (acme_sample_usage_window.csv) — drop in a week of minute-level counts if you have it.

Thanks — Neha

--

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeworks.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@acmeworks.com
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosted pricing follow-up & burst/peak profile

Thanks Neha — useful recap. A few clarifications:

1) Monthly pick: low/likely/high = 30M / 45M / 60M tokens. Likely is 45M.
2) Bursts: the 120 req/s are usually internal load tests or promotional tests we run before a release; historically they last 10–20 minutes. We do, however, run a few customer-facing campaigns that drive sustained traffic for ~1–2 hours and reach ~80–90 req/s.
3) We'll attach a week of minute-level traffic for the US region; engineering will sanitize but should be able to send something by tomorrow EOD PDT.

Unit economics question: what's a realistic target $/1M tokens (list vs committed) you can show for the 45M/month profile? We want to model this into the pilot budget. Also please call out any P95/P99 latency SLOs that map to each pricing lane.

—Lisa
Director, Product Ops
Acme Works
lisa.chen@acmeworks.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeworks.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Hosted pricing bands + quick SLA mapping (draft)

Lisa / Neha — looping in a short draft of pricing bands and SLA mapping. Attaching two files: hosted_pricing_bands_v2.xlsx (simple band table + example $/1M math) and SLA_credit_guidance.pdf. High level:

Pricing highlights (draft, targeted for 45M tokens/month)
- Pay-as-you-go (no commit): $85 / 1M tokens (list example)
- 3-month committed slab (45M/mo): $62–68 / 1M tokens depending on burst buffer & 99th pct latency target
- 12-month reserved (45M/mo committed): $45–55 / 1M tokens + burst package (short bursts to 2x sustained)

SLA/Latency mapping (examples)
- Standard hosted lane: P95 < 400ms token latency, P99 < 1.1s; no dedicated capacity, best-effort burst handling.
- Reserved lane (committed): P95 < 250ms, P99 < 700ms; burst buffer and prioritization in routing.

Other notes
- We recommend a 3-month ramp with a 1-month trial slab so you can validate real user UX before signing for 12 months.
- If you need us to model dollar impact for a 2-hour campaign that hits 90 req/s, send an expected campaign profile and we will produce a spend estimate (tokens, dollars, SLA exposure).

Marissa
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

(attachments: hosted_pricing_bands_v2.xlsx, SLA_credit_guidance.pdf)

Thanks Lisa — appreciate the quick answers and the expected CSV. Next steps from Redwood:

1) Marissa will finalize a 2-option commercial (3-month pilot slab vs 12-month reserved) with the explicit $/1M tokens tied to the 45M/month likely profile and a separate run-rate view that models the 90 req/s 2-hour campaign. Expect that by EOD today.
2) Karthik: can you put together a short note on routing/prioritization behavior during burst windows and how we treat experimental bursts vs production (for SLA math)? Karthik will add that to the quote packet.
3) Lisa: once you drop the minute-level CSV we will run a short sizing pass and include a recommended burst buffer (and a wallet for超 short experiments) in the quote.

We are aiming to have a pricing packet + an optional PO-ready SOW by early next week if the CSV arrives tomorrow.

If helpful, I can do a short 15-minute call with your engineering team to validate the sample CSV mapping to tokens/reqs — say a slot tomorrow at 11:30am PDT?

Best — Neha
